A form is made of fields, and each field of a widget; around them stand the objects that join a field to one form, check its value and draw it (`django/forms/fields.py:Field`, `django/forms/widgets.py:Widget`).
`Field` here is `django/forms/fields.py:Field`; a model's field is a different class, which makes one of these.*

The class's metaclass, `DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass`, takes every attribute that is a field out of the class body before the class is made, so that BerthForm has no attribute named ship, and collects them, after those of its bases, in a dictionary, `BaseForm.base_fields` ([Declaring a form: `DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass` and `BaseForm`](forms/declaring.md)) (`django/forms/forms.py:DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass`).

Each instance then deep-copies that dictionary into a `fields` of its own, each field with its widget, so that one form can change its fields without changing them for every other; a comment at the copy says so (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).
A form is **bound** when it is made with data or files, even an empty dictionary, and **unbound** otherwise (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).

A form is asked for one of its fields by name, `form["tonnage"]`, and answers with a **bound field**, a `BoundField` that joins the field to this form; it is made the first time it is asked for and kept (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__getitem__`).

`BaseForm.errors` calls `BaseForm.full_clean` if the errors are not yet known, and `BaseForm.is_valid` asks a bound form for them; once made, they are kept (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.errors`, `django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.is_valid`).

`BaseForm.errors` calls `BaseForm.full_clean` if the errors are not yet known, and `BaseForm.is_valid` asks a bound form for them; once made, they are kept (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.errors`, `django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.is_valid`).

Most widgets look their name up in the data; a checkbox that was not ticked is not in the data at all and reads as `False`, and a widget made of several inputs reads several names ([Widgets: `Widget` and its subclasses](forms/widgets.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.value_from_datadict`).
`Field.run_validators` calls every validator of the field on a value that is not empty, and gathers all their errors (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.clean`).

A value that passes goes into `cleaned_data`; a `ValidationError` from any step goes into the form's errors under the field's name, by way of `BaseForm.add_error`, and the field is left out of `cleaned_data` (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm._clean_fields`).

Last comes `BaseForm._post_clean`, which does nothing on a plain form and is where a model form fills its instance and has it validated (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm._clean_form`) ([Validation: `full_clean`, `cleaned_data` and the errors](forms/validation.md)).

The message is the validator's own, because the field's `error_messages` has none for its code, `"min_value"`; a field's message for a code replaces a validator's ([Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](forms/validators.md)) (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.run_validators`).

`str(form)` calls `RenderableMixin.render`, which has the form's **renderer** render a template with a context that the form makes, and marks the result safe (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableMixin.render`).

By default that is `django.forms.renderers.DjangoTemplates`, which keeps a template engine of its own, apart from those of `TEMPLATES`, that finds templates in `django/forms/templates/` and in the installed applications (`django/forms/renderers.py:get_default_renderer`, `django/forms/renderers.py:EngineMixin.engine`).

An unbound form shows each field's initial value; a bound one ordinarily shows the data that was submitted, as it was typed, and not the cleaned value, though a disabled field and a file field show their initial value still (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.value`, `django/forms/fields.py:Field.bound_data`).

The `"min"` came from the field, which put it on its widget when the field was made (`django/forms/fields.py:IntegerField.widget_attrs`).

The bound field added the rest as it drew: `"required"` because the field is required, and `"aria-invalid"` and `"aria-describedby"` because it has errors (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`); then the `"id"`, from the form's `auto_id`, `"id_%s"` unless the form is given another (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.as_widget`).

A bound formset makes as many forms as that count says, but never more than a limit, `BaseFormSet.absolute_max`, which a comment calls protection against a client that would have the server make any number of forms (`django/forms/formsets.py:BaseFormSet.total_form_count`).

A formset is valid when each of its forms is valid, those marked for deletion aside, and it has no errors of its own: a management form missing or invalid, too many or too few forms, or what its `clean` raised (`django/forms/formsets.py:BaseFormSet.is_valid`).

Its metaclass, `ModelFormMetaclass`, reads `Meta`, refuses one that names a model but neither `fields` nor `exclude` (`django/forms/models.py:ModelFormMetaclass.__new__`), and asks each model field it is to use for a form field, ordinarily by calling the model field's `formfield`, which makes the field's `blank` into `required`, its `verbose_name` into the label and its default into the initial value (`django/forms/models.py:fields_for_model`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.formfield`).

A model form made with an instance takes its initial values from the instance's fields (`django/forms/models.py:model_to_dict`).

`BaseModelForm.save` saves the instance and then its many-to-many values; with `commit=False` it returns the instance unsaved and gives the form a method, `BaseModelForm.save_m2m`, to call when the instance has been saved (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelForm.save`).
